title: Ending apartment vacation rentals and hotel rezoning of 48 properties
summary: On Sept. 29, the Council heard Resolution 26-129, which would send some apartment-zoned coastal properties forward for possible permanent hotel zoning. The Office of Hawaiian Affairs and a resident opposed it, the Realtors Association of Maui supported it, and an amendment was postponed.

upcomingEvent.what: Commission must report to the council

timeline.text: A proposed amendment to the resolution was postponed until the Council takes up Committee Report 26-68.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: One resident opposed the resolution, saying “we are in a housing crisis.”
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The Realtors Association of Maui testified in support of the resolution.

timeline.text: Resolution 26-129 would send some apartment-zoned coastal properties forward for possible permanent hotel zoning.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The Office of Hawaiian Affairs opposed Resolution 26-129, which could move apartment-zoned coastal properties toward hotel zoning.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: A council member said the Planning Commission approved five of 48 properties from an earlier resolution.
timeline.body: County Council Meeting

timeline.text: The main motion passed with five yes votes, including one abstention, and one no.

Recommendation to the council on the two rezoning resolutions: The commission voted to recommend approval for the variance, all-timeshare and one Hāna property, and denial for the other property groups.
Recommendation that the council explore the use of public funds for the purpose of housing: The commission voted to ask the council to explore using public funds for housing.
A separate motion asked the council to explore using public funds for housing.

Friendly amendment requiring shoreline properties to get a certified shoreline survey within two years: A commissioner's proposal to require certified shoreline surveys for shoreline properties did not get a second.
The commission recommended denial for single-owner, mixed timeshare, leasehold and hotel-like properties.
The final motion recommends approving the two variance and two all-timeshare properties.
A friendly amendment added a hotel-like property in Hāna for approval.
Staff said he will transfer the motion information to the council.
A commissioner said the commission lacked enough information to evaluate the properties.
A Lahaina Community Land Trust staff member urged returning non-hotel units to housing.
The president of the Maui Sunset timeshare association supported hotel zoning for that property.
The Office of Hawaiian Affairs opposed both resolutions.
Staff said some of the properties now have owner-occupied or long-term rental units.
The commission must report to the council by November 24, 2026.
Staff said their sole purpose is to let these properties keep vacation rentals.
Two council bills would move about 48 apartment-zoned properties into new hotel zoning districts.
Staff will take a report back to the council, which will decide on the bills at a future meeting.
The commission reviewed two council resolutions to rezone specific properties into new H3 and H4 hotel districts.
Staff said the only change in hotel zoning is allowing vacation rental use to continue.
Bill 9 ends vacation rentals in apartment districts by December 31, 2028, in West Maui and December 31, 2030, elsewhere.
Bill 9 aimed to end vacation rentals in apartment districts to expand long-term housing.
Motion to adopt Resolution 26-130: A motion to adopt Resolution 26-130 was on the floor when the recording ended, with no vote heard.
